title: Acid-catalysed ester hydrolysis
subtitle: H₃O⁺ protonates the ester, water adds, protons shuttle, ethanol leaves

reactants.caption: ethyl acetate + H₃O⁺ + water
reactants.learnerPrompt: Water is a weak nucleophile. First activate the ester.
hintTiers: An acid makes a carbonyl group more electrophilic. Which oxygen of the ester is the best base?
The carbonyl oxygen takes a proton from H₃O⁺; that O–H bonding pair stays on water's oxygen. Two arrows.
Carbonyl oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to a proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → lone pair on the oxygen of H₃O⁺.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Water attacks a neutral ester only very slowly. Protonate the carbonyl oxygen first to make the carbon more electrophilic.
The OEt oxygen is less basic: its lone pairs are shared with the C=O group. Protonating the carbonyl oxygen gives a cation stabilised by both oxygens.

protonated-ester.caption: protonated ester + water
hintTiers: The protonated carbonyl group is now a strong electrophile. Which molecule is the nucleophile?
A lone pair of water forms a bond to the carbonyl carbon, and the C=O π pair moves onto the protonated oxygen. Two arrows.
Water's oxygen lone pair → new O–C bond to the carbonyl carbon; C=O π bond → lone pair on the protonated oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Electrons flow towards the electronegative atom. The C=O π pair moves onto oxygen.
Removing that proton just goes back to the start. Use the activated ester: water attacks the carbonyl carbon.

first-adduct.caption: tetrahedral intermediate (protonated on the added water)
first-adduct.learnerPrompt: Move a proton off the positive oxygen.
hintTiers: The oxygen that came from water carries a positive charge. Which molecule can take one of its protons?
A water molecule uses a lone pair on one of those O–H protons; that O–H bonding pair stays on the oxygen. Two arrows.
Water's oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to a proton on the positive oxygen; that O–H bond → lone pair on that oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Losing water just reverses the addition. To move forwards, take a proton off the positive oxygen.
Ethoxide is a poor leaving group, and it cannot exist in acid. The oxygen needs a proton before it can leave as ethanol.

tetrahedral.caption: neutral tetrahedral intermediate + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: Ethoxide is a poor leaving group, ethanol a good one. Which oxygen should be protonated?
The OEt oxygen takes a proton from H₃O⁺; the O–H bonding pair stays on water's oxygen. Two arrows.
Lone pair of the OEt oxygen → new O–H bond to a proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → lone pair on water's oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Ethoxide is a poor leaving group and cannot form in acid. Protonate the OEt oxygen first, so that ethanol leaves.
Protonating an OH group lets water leave, which only takes you back towards the ester. Protonate the OEt oxygen.

protonated-tetrahedral.caption: tetrahedral intermediate protonated on the OEt oxygen
hintTiers: Ethanol is now a good leaving group. Which electrons push it out?
An OH lone pair re-forms a C=O π bond, and the C–O bond to the positive oxygen breaks. Two arrows.
Lone pair of an OH oxygen → new C=O π bond; C–O bond to the protonated OEt oxygen → lone pair on that oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Removing that proton undoes the last step. The protonated oxygen is now ready to leave as ethanol.
That OH oxygen has no proton to make it a good leaving group. The protonated OEt oxygen leaves, as ethanol.

protonated-acid.caption: protonated acetic acid + ethanol + water
hintTiers: The product is protonated. Which molecule takes the proton?
Water uses a lone pair on the proton of the positive oxygen; that O–H bonding pair stays on that oxygen. Two arrows.
Water's oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton on the positive oxygen; that O–H bond → lone pair on the carbonyl oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Ethanol adding again is the reverse reaction. Water is in large excess, so the equilibrium moves on: remove the proton.
Ethanol could take the proton, but water is the solvent and far more plentiful. Use water to regenerate H₃O⁺.

steps.explanationAfterStep: Protonating the carbonyl oxygen gives a cation shared between both oxygens and carbon: a much better electrophile for a weak nucleophile like water.
Water adds to the carbonyl carbon: a tetrahedral intermediate.
Water takes the extra proton: a neutral tetrahedral intermediate and H₃O⁺.
Protonating the OEt oxygen turns a poor leaving group (ethoxide) into a good one (ethanol).
An OH lone pair re-forms the C=O bond and ethanol leaves.
Water takes the proton and H₃O⁺ is regenerated: it is a catalyst. Every step is reversible; a large excess of water drives the hydrolysis to the acid.

mechanismSummary: H₃O⁺ protonates the carbonyl oxygen of ethyl acetate and water adds. Proton transfers move a proton from the added water to the OEt oxygen, so ethanol can leave as an OH lone pair re-forms C=O. Water removes the last proton and the acid catalyst is regenerated. Every step is reversible: excess water favours hydrolysis.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 10
